prompts.a: A cast-iron pan is taken out of an oven and left to cool in a kitchen. Its temperature, in degrees Celsius, is modeled by $T(t)=24+176e^{-0.04t}$, where $t$ is the time in minutes since the pan was taken out of the oven. Show that $T$ satisfies the differential equation $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-0.04\,(T-24)$.
prompts.b: Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve $y=T(t)$ at $t=10$. Use this tangent line to approximate the temperature of the pan at $t=15$.
prompts.c: Is the approximation in part (b) less than or greater than the actual temperature $T(15)$? Use $\dfrac{d^2T}{dt^2}$ to justify your answer.
prompts.d: The pan can be handled safely once its temperature reaches $100$ degrees Celsius. Find the time $t$ at which $T(t)=100$. Then, using correct units, find the rate of change of the temperature of the pan at that time.

prompts.a: A sealed capsule holds $18$ grams of a radioactive tracer. Let $M(t)$ be the mass of the tracer, in grams, remaining $t$ years after the capsule is sealed. The rate at which the mass decreases is proportional to the mass present, so $\frac{dM}{dt}=-kM$ for a positive constant $k$. Use separation of variables to find an expression for $M(t)$ in terms of $k$. Show the work that leads to your answer.
prompts.b: The half-life of the tracer is $4$ years, that is, $M(4)=\frac12 M(0)$. Find $k$.
prompts.c: Using the value of $k$ from part (b), at what time $t$ will $6$ grams of the tracer remain? Express your answer in terms of natural logarithms.
prompts.d: Find the average mass of the tracer in the capsule over the time interval $0\le t\le 8$ years. Show the setup, and give your answer in grams, in exact form.
